Notes: Year Established basis: earliest documented Jewish presence at Berenice itself is this decree of 'the archons and the politeuma of the Jews at Berenice' (CJZC 70 = SEG 16.931 = IBerenike 18) honouring Decimus Valerius Dionysios son of Gaius for paying to plaster the floor and paint the walls of the amphitheater (the community's meeting place); exempted from liturgies and crowned at assemblies and the New Moon. Dated 8-6 BCE by the Posen Library (Levine's translation); midpoint -7, c. (Harland AGRW 305: late 1st c. BCE; IRCyr reads year 23 or 25 of the Actian era). Presence only, no count: an organized, self-governing community with several archons and a wealthy benefactor stratum. Context not used as rows: Josephus (Against Apion 2.44) says Ptolemy I sent Jews to 'Cyrene and the other cities of Libya' (regional, Berenice not named; the 1906 Jewish Encyclopedia infers Berenice's Jewish settlement dates from Ptolemy I, but this is not documented for the site); Euesperides was refounded/relocated as Berenice in the mid-3rd c. BCE; Applebaum (1979, p.160, via Wikipedia) reportedly places a Jewish community there near the city's founding, not verified.

Decree of the archons and politeuma of the Judeans in Berenike (CJZC 71 = IBerenike 17 = CIG 5361) honouring the Roman official Marcus Tittius son of Sextus, passed at the assembly of the Feast of Tabernacles, year 55, 25 Phaophi; to be set up in the most prominent place in the amphitheater. Nine archons named (Kleandros son of Stratonikos, Euphranor son of Ariston, Sosigenes son of Sosippos, Andromachos son of Andromachos, Marcus Laeilius Onasion son of Apollonios, Philonides son of Hagemon, Autokles son of Zenon, Sonikos son of Theodotos, Josepos son of Straton). Date per Harland: 24 CE if Actian era (preferred, because a Roman citizen sits among the archons) or 41 BCE if Cyrenaican era; the 1906 Jewish Encyclopedia and Encyclopaedia Judaica give 13 BCE (Boeckh's calculation). Presence only: organized politeuma observing Sukkot; mostly Greek names (Hellenized community).

Inscription (CJZC 72 = SEG 17.823 = IBerenike 16): 'the synagogue of the Judeans in Berenike' decided to inscribe on Parian stone the names of contributors to the restoration (repair) of the synagogue building; dated year 2 of Nero, 6 Choiak (56 CE per Harland; IRCyr gives December 55 CE). 18 named donors: 10 archons, a priest (Kartisthenes) and 7 others including two women; donors are a subset, not a population count. Presence: an established community with its own synagogue building old enough to need restoration; mostly Greek names.

Event, regional (Berenice not named): after the fall of Jerusalem the Sicarius Jonathan, a weaver, led poor Jews of 'the cities of Cyrene' into the desert; Catullus, governor of the Libyan Pentapolis (which included Berenice), suppressed them and then had 'all the rich and wealthy Jews' slain, 'no fewer in all than three thousand' (Josephus, War 7.11.1-2), confiscating their property. The 3000 is a death toll across the Pentapolis/Cyrene, not Berenice's population; c. 73 CE.
